key_claim: An estimated 7.4 million Americans aged 65+ are living with Alzheimer's; total dementia care costs will reach a record $409 billion in 2026 (up $25 billion year on year); yet only 14% of adults report ever having discussed brain health with their doctor, and the report flags growing shortages across the dementia-care workforce.
notes: Tier 2 major data provider (Association report, also published in the journal Alzheimer's & Dementia). Anchor for US scale, cost, latent diagnostic demand and workforce shortage.

title: Labcorp launches FDA-cleared blood test to support initial Alzheimer's disease assessment in primary care
date_evidence: Labcorp launches FDA-cleared blood test to support initial Alzheimer's disease assessment in primary care ... 5 May 2026 ... Elecsys pTau-181 ... the first and only blood test cleared by the FDA to aid in the initial assessment of Alzheimer's disease in the primary care setting ... 2,200 patient service centers ... 97.9% negative predictive value ... helps reduce unnecessary referrals amid a national shortage of neurologists.
key_claim: Labcorp made Roche's FDA-cleared Elecsys pTau-181 blood test - the first cleared for the primary care setting - available nationwide across more than 2,200 US patient service centres, offering a 97.9% negative predictive value and explicitly intended to help rule out Alzheimer's and reduce unnecessary specialist referrals amid a national shortage of neurologists.
notes: Tier 3 specialist trade press. Anchor for the primary-care diagnostic rollout (the 'what's changing' core) and the neurologist-shortage capacity point.

title: NICE opens consultation on previously-rejected Alzheimer's treatments donanemab and lecanemab
date_evidence: 01 April 2026 ... The consultation, published on 31 March 2026, follows an appeal by the manufacturers ... NICE said it would not recommend the drugs for NHS use for a third time ... The consultation will close on 28 April 2026. The committee will meet again on 10 June 2026.
key_claim: NICE opened a third consultation (31 March 2026) on donanemab and lecanemab after rejecting them for NHS use three times; the drugs delay progression from mild to moderate Alzheimer's by about 4-6 months but require regular infusions, frequent MRI monitoring and intensive side-effect surveillance, and have been judged not cost-effective; a further committee meeting is set for 10 June 2026.
notes: Tier 3 specialist trade press (Royal College of Pharmacy). Anchor for the treatment-funding gap: diagnosis routes UK patients to drugs NICE will not fund, with high infusion/MRI/monitoring demands.
